Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost baseline + mapping for hosted → reserved/private

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we evaluate Redwood for customer-facing features, procurement has asked for a clear baseline and a simple crosswalk: what does our cost look like on Hosted (your public API) today versus if we moved to Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or a Private deployment?

Specifically, can you provide:
- A one-page baseline (per-1M tokens example) for Hosted with current list prices
- A mapping showing which line items change for Dedicated and Private (e.g., compute, storage, networking, support, SLA uplift)
- Typical discount ranges by commit (12/24/36 months) and recommended minimums to see price parity with Hosted at scale

We need the doc by EOD Wednesday — our procurement cycle is tight and we want to include this in the vendor comparison pack. Also flag any operational prerequisites for Private (VPC, KMS, on-prem options).

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Corp

P.S. Procurement copied for visibility — feel free to include financial contacts in replies.
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Velez <elena.velez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost baseline + mapping for hosted → reserved/private

Hi Elena — great to connect earlier. Attached is a concise crosswalk and an example workbook that walks through a 1M-token and 10M-token scenario (file: service_tier_cost_crosswalk.xlsx). High level summary below:

Hosted (baseline)
- Unit: per 1k input+output tokens; simple metered billing
- Primary cost drivers: model size + tokens, KV-cache miss rate, streaming overhead
- Typical use: low-friction, pay-as-you-go; no infra commitments

Dedicated (reserved pool)
- Changes: compute becomes a committed resource (GPU-hours), predictable throughput; per-token engine cost falls with better batching and KV cache locality
- Add-ons: Autoscaling buffer, burst credits, optional SLA uplift
- Pricing impact: list rate per-token replaced by reserved capacity monthly fee + lower per-token egress on large workloads

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Changes: moved to a platform fee + infra (BYO or Redwood-managed) + enterprise support; includes longer onboarding and security configs (KMS, routing)
- Pricing impact: higher base (platform + infra) but lower marginal per-token cost at very high sustained volume

Discounting & commitments (examples)
- 12 mo commit: 10–18% off hosted list (depends on model mix & burst profile)
- 24 mo commit: 18–28%
- 36 mo / strategic: 25–40% with reserved GPU pooling and capacity sharing

Attachments included: service_tier_cost_crosswalk.xlsx, pilot-sow-template.docx (SOW we use for PoVs).

Next steps:
1) I can walk procurement through the workbook tomorrow (Tue) at 10am PT — does that work?
2) Ben and Aditya are looped for technical and pricing details.

Thanks — sending the workbook now.

— Monica
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Cc: Elena Velez <elena.velez@acmecorp.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Cost baseline + mapping for hosted → reserved/private

Quick clarifying questions for procurement before the walkthrough:
- Do you have a sense of peak qps and typical seq length? Batching and KV cache hit rate change the crossover point by a lot.
- For Dedicated: are you considering Redwood-managed GPU pools or customer-hosted (e.g., on your cloud account)? Our pricing differs (managed carries a small ops premium).

Operational note: for Private, add ~6–8 weeks for network validation and KMS integration on our standard onboarding — call that out if timelines are tight.

Thanks,
Ben
Pricing & GTM

To: Elena Velez <elena.velez@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 08:46 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick clarifying questions for procurement before the walkthrough:
> - Do you have a sense of peak qps and typical seq length? Batching and KV cache hit rate change the crossover point by a lot.
> - For Dedicated: are you considering Redwood-managed GPU pools or customer-hosted (e.g., on your cloud account)? Our pricing differs (managed carries a small ops premium).

Adding a short technical appendix you can paste into procurement: (see kernel-mapping-note.pdf)
- Cost drivers: sustained GPU-hours, peak concurrency (affects number of replicas), and model variant (float vs quantized).
- Typical savings on Dedicated: 20–45% per-token once you sustain above ~3k concurrent tokens/sec for the most common chat workloads (higher for steady seq-length workloads).
- Private on-prem: biggest savings if you can fully utilize reserved hardware (multi-tenant inference across teams) — but needs reliable utilization to be cost-effective.
- Caveat: inference latency SLOs may require extra lower-latency replicas (increases cost).

If you can share a sample 7-day trace (anonymized tokens/seq-dist), we can run a quick simulation to show crossover points (I can turn this around in 48 hours).

— Aditya
Applied ML / Serving Optimization
From: Elena Velez <elena.velez@acmecorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost baseline + mapping for hosted → reserved/private

Thanks — this is helpful and the workbook is clear. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:
- Acme is willing to run a 90-day pilot (PoV). Would Redwood provide a starter credit for the pilot? We typically ask for 20–30% credits to offset evaluation cost.
- If the pilot is successful, we are likely to consider a 24-month reserved commit. Can you outline a conversion incentive (one-time credit or step discount) if we convert from pilot to reserved within 90 days?
- For Private: we'd like a preliminary checklist of the minimum infra/responsibilities to evaluate internal readiness (network, KMS, NDR).

If you can confirm those three items in writing, procurement will slot Redwood into the vendor shortlist. Looking forward to the walkthrough tomorrow.

— Elena
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Corp
